items.note: その (sono) modifies a following noun ('that ___'); unlike それ (sore) from an earlier lesson, which stands alone as a pronoun ('that one'), その can't be used by itself. Compare この (kono) and あの (ano) for the same pronoun-vs-determiner pattern with これ (kore) and あれ (are).
Counter ほん (hon)/ぼん (bon)/ぽん (pon) for long, slender objects like bottles. Watch this one by ear: にほん (ni-hon) here is 'two long objects', identical in sound to にほん (nihon, 'Japan') from Lesson 1.
Counter まい (mai) for thin, flat objects

items.note: あの (ano) modifies a following noun ('that ___ over there'); unlike あれ (are) from an earlier lesson, which stands alone as a pronoun ('that one over there'), あの can't be used by itself. Compare この (kono) and その (sono) for the same pattern with これ (kore) and それ (sore).
A regular い-adjective placed directly before its noun, e.g. あおいTシャツ (aoi tii-shatsu); unlike あか (aka) or しろ (shiro), あお never drops its い to form a special wine compound — there's no あおワイン.

Suffix — the general-purpose counter, used when no specific counter fits. Attaches to native-Japanese numerals (ひと〜 (hito-), ふた〜 (futa-), みっ〜 (mit-) → ひとつ (hitotsu), ふたつ (futatsu), みっつ (mittsu)). Written 〜つ (~tsu).

items.note: Red (base adjective form); compare あかワイン (aka wain) (red wine), which is NOT あかい (akai) ワイン (wain) — see that card for the exception
くろい (kuroi) is a regular い-adjective placed before its noun, e.g. くろいくつ (kuroi kutsu, 'black shoes'). Unlike あか (aka) and しろ (shiro), くろ has no special wine compound — there's no くろワイン.
Like あか (aka) in あかワイン (akawain, 'red wine'), しろ drops its い before ワイン: しろワイン (shirowain), 'white wine' — but keeps the full しろい form as a regular adjective before any other noun.

items.reviewNote: Shown in plain parentheses (not the wave-dash 〜 convention) rather than a separate sub-entry.
items.note: Dish, plate. お (o) is an optional polite prefix, shown here in plain parentheses
コップ (koppu) is the general word for a drinking glass or cup; contrast マグカップ (magukappu), a mug specifically, and コーヒーカップ (koohii kappu), a coffee cup typically served with a saucer.
Base reading of the floor counter — after most numbers (1 いっ (ik), 2 に (ni), 4 よん (yon), 5 ご (go), 6 ろっ (rok) …), e.g. ごかい (gokai) (5th floor)
Voiced (dakuten) form of the floor counter — after さん (san) (3), e.g. さんがい (sangai) (3rd floor)
Uses the voiced がい (gai) form after さん (san) — さんがい (sangai) — rather than the plain かい (kai) counter used after most other numbers.
Specifically a mug (from English 'mug cup'); contrast the more general コップ (koppu, glass/cup) and コーヒーカップ (kōhīkappu), a coffee cup typically served with a saucer.
A mikan is a satsuma / Japanese mandarin — a small, sweet, seedless, easy-to-peel citrus, extremely popular in Japan and a winter staple

Fixed compound noun, NOT あかい (akai) ワイン (wain). Contrast the regular い-adjective+noun pattern, which keeps the い (i): あかい (akai) シャツ (shatsu) (“red shirt”), あおい (aoi) Tシャツ (T-shatsu) (“blue T-shirt”). Only these set colour-compounds drop it: あかワイン (aka wain) (“red wine”), しろワイン (shiro wain) (“white wine”).

items.note: どこ (doko) alone asks a location ('where is it?'), but どこの (doko no) asks origin or make — here, 'what place's coffee cup,' i.e. where it's from. The の (no) turns the location word into a modifier of the noun that follows.

items.note: の (no) here stands in for the omitted noun ('coffee cup') — literally 'the one from England', a common way to avoid repeating something already mentioned.

items.note: Uses むっつ, the general-purpose つ-counter, rather than a shape-specific counter like the ほん used for bottles in this lesson's そのワインを２ほんください — つ covers everyday objects like cups when no dedicated counter fits.
